diagnosis.E1_pillar1_descent: Root cause found on the collision model (tests/test_nefarian_ledge_drop_floor_query.py port of the BIH first-hit query). The plan does propose pillar_descent_step_off at local (-15.8,-32.4) z 9.37 (new replay in test_nefarian_stranded.py). Pillar 1 lies wholly in the platform's north half (local y<0), where the unlimited first-hit floor query used by ProbeLedgeDrop and MotionMaster::MoveFall returns the model underside (local z -8.666) for every candidate, so ChooseStepOff ends with ledge_drop_landing_height_mismatch every decision and ExecuteFall would refuse too. No heading around pillar 1 escapes it; pillar 0 fails on headings -90..0 deg, which its slot headings avoid; pillar 2 is fine. Fix = shared executor (patch request 1). Refused plan steps are now traced as nefarian_move_refused:<mechanic>:<reason>.
diagnosis.E2_shafts_and_board: The elevator model is a closed body (walk surface, bottom at local -8.666, outer wall 69.6-71.2 yd); the pillars are hollow shafts open into it. The recorded positions (<=1.5 yd from centre, local z 3-4) are inside a shaft, which only unproven native chase can reach. No executor-proven swim/jump/walk leaves a shaft (two-sided collision, no floor until the bottom), so an emerge/board step there would be refused every decision: the plan names the state (nefarian_inside_pillar_column / nefarian_inside_platform_body) and OnPillarStructure excludes the shaft. Prevention: in phase 2 every plan now carries nefarian_pillar_hold[:diag], alone or as the fallback beside a step; the dispatch stops the member and renews the Mechanic movement lease exactly like the platform hold, so native chase cannot walk anyone into a shaft or onto a top unboarded. A non-passenger on a top boards at the lowered stop and, during the rise, while the top is within the 0.5-yd emerge band; past it nefarian_rising_top_missed.
diagnosis.E3_bone_warriors: The chase model found a real planner flaw: the shackler held the warrior on Nefarian's tank inside his front and the handler ignored held warriors, so breath refilled it every 18 s (46 s active, reproduced). Now ShackleCandidate never takes a warrior in the front, LooseWarrior takes a warrior held in the front, and warriors near a pillar rank as urgent as those in the front. WarriorFrontMarginDeg/WarriorDanger/WarriorPointSafe moved unchanged from Movement.h to Tactics.h. Acceptance observation: BotNefarianWarriorWatch.h reports once per warrior an active span >45 s or a warrior on a pillar structure, recorded by one reporter per cohort as decision-trace actions nefarian_bone_warrior_active_over_45s / nefarian_bone_warrior_on_pillar; added to the research contract's acceptance_observations and dossier section 9.
diagnosis.E4_hunter_min_range: Standoff specs (hunters) keep 5 + dragon melee reach + 1.5 yd (29.33 on Nefarian, 27.33 on Onyxia) from their dragon target in the sighted formation spot (<=36 yd); SurfaceGoal.SightMinRangeYards makes a drifted-in hunter's spot stop serving so it corrects outward. Phase 3's old 18-yd ranged slot was inside 27.83.
diagnosis.E5_class_logic: Unchanged. Re-measure after the round-3 run: warlock Life Tap loop, mage mana gate (both pin artefacts), and hunter damage in phase 2, where no pillar-top spot is outside the prototype's 12.2-yd minimum range (hunter can only melee there).

patch_requests.why: E1: bound the ledge-drop landing query and the Fall stage's floor query to the declared drop (Z_OFFSET_FIND_HEIGHT + (z - declared landing) + tolerance) and launch the fall onto that proven floor (MoveFall's body with that height). Under the Nefarian platform's north half the unlimited first-hit query returns the model underside, so no pillar-1 step-off (and no stranded fall there) can ever be admitted. A bounded first-hit query visits the same BIH leaves but no triangle beyond the bound, so wherever the unlimited query found the declared floor it returns the same height: results only change where the executor refused before (Magmaw/Stonecore/calibration unaffected; they do not use this surface executor's ledge drop or, where they do, their drops already matched). 116-line unified diff, file grows 550 -> 591 lines; `git apply --check` passes on c8e8bfe85b.
patch_requests.tests: Already in tests/test_nefarian_ledge_drop_floor_query.py (pass now, they model the query on the vmo): test_pillar_one_rim_every_step_off_lands_on_the_underside_unbounded (reproduces the refusal), test_pillar_one_rim_bounded_search_lands_on_the_ring (the patch formula admits the first footprint-clear candidate <=1.5 yd out and the fall from there lands on the ring under the 14.57-yd threshold), test_bounded_search_changes_nothing_where_the_first_hit_was_right (pillar 2 and the round-5 orb-ledge drop give identical heights). Suggested source guard after applying: assert in tests/test_nefarian_stop_hold.py-style text check that ProbeLedgeDrop and ExecuteFall call LedgeDropLandingSearchYards and ExecuteFall returns LaunchFallOnto(bot, floor).

needs_user_decision.question: Nefarian phase 2: a bot that native movement pushed inside a hollow pillar shaft (round 2: the rogue in 3/3 runs, both tanks in 2/3) cannot leave it by any movement the server's collision proves. How should such a bot be handled?
options: Prevention only: the new phase-2 pillar hold stops the native chase that puts bots there; a bot already inside is held with the typed state nefarian_inside_pillar_column and is lost for the fight

Allow a client-like exit: let a swimmer inside a shaft swim straight up through the pillar top (treating the shaft's inner faces as non-colliding, as a WoW client's one-sided collision may), then board; needs a shared-executor exception to the line-of-sight proof
Treat a bot inside a shaft as an infrastructure/terminal failure of the attempt (watchdog stop) instead of fighting on without it
needs_user_decision.recommendation: Prevention only for round 3, then look at whether any bot still ends up in a shaft. The second option weakens a lawfulness proof on the strength of an unverified claim about client collision.
needs_user_decision.context: Collision-model evidence: tests/test_nefarian_ledge_drop_floor_query.py::test_the_platform_is_a_closed_body_with_hollow_pillar_shafts. The coordinator's request asked for an emerge/board step. Emerge (the swimmer's board report) requires the platform surface within 0.5 yd of the feet, but a shaft has no surface for 6+ yd, so such a step would be refused every decision. The bot is shown as a typed hold instead. Dossier section 7f.

The standoff band on Nefarian is 29.3–36 yd. Where fires or pillars leave no serving spot in it, the hunter falls back to the old unsighted spot and can still take some min-range rejections.

The shared patch changes the ledge-drop admission for every encounter that uses the transport-surface executor. It is designed to change only cases that were refused before, and a test pins this for pillar 2 and the orb-ledge drop. Still, the coordinator should run the shared ledge-drop tests after applying it.
